description: We are team Xenonite who is passionate about astronomy / astrophysics and its integration in computational sciences. Skilled in programming languages python , C , C++ we have projects showcasing simulation for astronomical applications and embedded systems software features in spacecraft. Looking forward to meeting the community of people sharing the same passion for space as at the hackathon and connecting!
summary: Our project Intuition is a web based martian guide for the astronauts to navigate the following parameter during their EVA (ExtraVehicular Activity) on Mars : Temperature,Terrain,Pressure and Radiation. We have chosen Gale crater as the landing and exploration zone. The choice was made on the basis of data abundance and parameter feasibility. The current project simulates EVA sol 004 with visual dashboard showcasing 12 km of area with the path to be followed. We plan to extend the project by showcasing real time parameter changes and enabling the deployment of the software in a landscape length's arm mounted touchscreen hardware in the astronauts suit. Our main objective is it to create a software astronuats can easily and quickly access to guide them in the extremely complicated mars mission just like human intuition i.e quick witted , trustworthy and go to saviour.
details: Its a tool showing the following parameters at our chosen Gale crater (as landing and exploration zone) : Temperature, Terrain, Radiation and Pressure with a visual map. It shows a simulation for Sol 004 of the mission specifically EVA duration. Our goal is to create a helpful and quick accessibility software to guide the astronauts through their mission. Frontend is React 19.2 and TypeScript, Frontend CSS, HTML Canvas and SVG, Build scripts is Node.js, and local json was also used. We really focused on which area and parameter to choose, and we landed on Gale Crater since we believe the extensive data and terrain conditions are optimal for this project.However we did notice the shortcoming of this region due to its lack of scientific task feasibility (very low water content) and few other but after research on similar projects we found an award winning tool which utilised Gale crater data and later extended to other sites which inspired our choice and potential to extend it further to potential landing sites in the future.
